issues.legal_issue: The presumption arising from a person being unheard of for seven years does not establish the date of death, so a claimant whose title depends on death after a legally significant change must prove that timing.
material_facts: Two brothers acquired the disputed property as joint family property, and one brother was a coparcener.
The missing brother was last heard of in 1930, and his wife later sold an interest in the property to the plaintiffs’ predecessor.
The plaintiffs’ claimed interest depended on the missing brother having died after the relevant property law came into force, so that his wife acquired an interest.
The plaintiffs relied on the fact that the missing brother had not been heard of for more than seven years and produced no evidence establishing when he died.
The surviving coparcener later sold the property to the first defendant.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs did not prove that the missing brother died after the relevant law came into force. The presumption of death did not establish a particular date of death, so the wife was not shown to have acquired an interest to convey. The surviving coparcener was entitled to convey the property, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 107 and 108 of the Indian Evidence Act, proof that a person has not been heard of for seven years by those who would naturally have heard from him shifts the burden of proving that he is alive and supports a presumption of death when the question arises. It does not presume the date of death, whether during the seven-year period or at its end; a party whose claim depends on death at a particular time must prove that fact. The Court applied the Privy Council’s decision in Lal Chand Marwari v. Mahant Ramrup Gir, which states that the fact of death may be presumed but its timing is a matter of proof.

rule.if: property_title_appeal and person_unheard_seven_years and title_depends_on_death_after_legal_change and no_evidence_of_death_time and claimant_relies_only_on_absence

predicates.property_title_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning competing claims to title in property.
predicates.person_unheard_seven_years: A person was not heard of for at least seven years by people who would naturally have heard from that person if alive.
predicates.title_depends_on_death_after_legal_chang: A claimant's asserted property interest depends on the person's having died after a legally significant change.
predicates.no_evidence_of_death_time: The claimant offers no evidence establishing when the person died.
predicates.claimant_relies_only_on_absence: The claimant relies only on the person's prolonged absence to establish the timing of death.
predicates.claimant_cannot_establish_title_through_: The claimant cannot establish title through an interest allegedly acquired by the missing person's spouse.

issues.definition: When a property-title appeal depends on death after a legally significant change, prolonged absence alone, without evidence of the time of death, does not establish title through the missing person's spouse.
